solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Guessed amount of arsenic given to my boss

parts.note: As is the chemical symbol for arsenic
a sum is an amount, especially of money
the setter's boss is the crossword editor, ED for short

explanation.surface: Someone estimates a dose of poison slipped to their employer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amount of arsenic' reads as one idea, an 'As-sum', so the chemical symbol comes first. 'My boss' is the setter speaking: the editor who runs the crossword page.
explanation.definitionFit: To assume something is to suppose it without proof, so assumed works as a past tense meaning guessed.

clue.text: Regions claiming diverse rights to unpaid debts

indicators.note: claiming means taking in, and diverse says the two items are taken in at separate spots

parts.note: areas are regions
R is the abbreviation for right, and the plural gives two

explanation.surface: Several regions claim various rights over unpaid debts.
explanation.walkthrough: The two R's do not go in together: one lands after the first A, the other before the final S, which is what 'diverse' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrears are money owed that should already have been paid, so they are overdue debts.

clue.text: Dodge swindler, one replacing ace

indicators.note: replacing means one letter takes the place of another in the word

parts.note: a shark is a swindler or con artist
the Roman numeral for one
A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

explanation.surface: Someone avoids a con man who has swapped in a card for an ace.
explanation.definitionFit: To shirk is to avoid a duty or responsibility, so it means to dodge it.

clue.text: What widely secures graduate access to Yale?

definitions.text: What widely secures graduate access to Yale?

parts.words: What widely secures graduate access to Yale?
parts.note: surface reading: what gets a postgraduate into Yale University
setter's reading: a key that opens many Yale locks, its first word being a postgraduate degree title

explanation.surface: Asks what qualification gets a graduate admitted to Yale University.
explanation.walkthrough: Yale is both the American university and a brand of lock. A master's is a postgraduate degree, and a key that opens many locks widely gives access.
explanation.definitionFit: A master key opens a whole set of different locks, which is the widely granted access the clue describes.

clue.text: Doctor's surgery stops prescribing medicine?

indicators.note: to stop something is to plug it, so one piece fills the gap inside the other

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor, with the possessive S
an op is an operation, a piece of surgery

explanation.surface: A GP's practice stops issuing prescriptions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor's surgery' is the British name for a GP's practice; here the doctor's letters wrap round surgery in the sense of an operation.
explanation.definitionFit: Drops are liquid medicine given a few drips at a time, as for eyes or ears.

clue.text: First class support guards on board

indicators.note: something that guards another keeps it surrounded, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: a sling supports an injured arm
A1 means first class, written with the letter I standing for the figure 1

explanation.surface: A top-quality brace keeps a passenger safe aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is a classic shorthand for first-rate; crosswords freely swap the digit 1 for the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sailing is travelling by ship, that is aboard a vessel, so the phrase on board describes them.

clue.text: Bishop interrupting house party curtailed piece of music

indicators.note: curtailed means docked of its tail, so the last letter goes
to interrupt is to cut in between two things, so this piece sits between the others

parts.note: a semi is a semi-detached house, the common British home sharing one wall
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a revel is a lively party, before losing its last letter

explanation.surface: A bishop breaks into a cut-short house party during a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece of music' hints at a whole composition, but it is a single note.
explanation.definitionFit: A semibreve is a whole note in musical notation, a small unit or piece of written music.

clue.text: Suffer from return of former police force to province

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the letters read right to left

parts.note: the Royal Ulster Constabulary, Northern Ireland's police until 2001
NI is Northern Ireland, often called the Province

explanation.surface: Someone suffers as a disbanded police force comes back to Ulster.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are reversed together, as one string.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a loss or penalty is to bring it on oneself and so suffer it.

clue.text: Quick-tempered rector excluded from Barking libraries and clubs

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, so the letters go wild into a new order
excluded from means left out of, so one letter is removed

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for rector, to be removed
taken as written
C is the card abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: An angry clergyman is banned from the libraries and clubs of Barking, an east London town.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking looks like the east London place name; it is slang for crazy and stirs the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Irascible describes someone easily angered, which is what quick-tempered means.

clue.text: Disagree with soldier arresting a couple of Poles allegedly on vacation

indicators.note: to arrest is to take into custody, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
taken as written
N and S are the north and south poles

indicators.note: a word on vacation is emptied, so only its outer letters remain

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word allegedly

explanation.surface: Someone disputes a story that a soldier detained two Polish holidaymakers.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital P makes 'Poles' look like people from Poland, but it means the magnetic poles; 'allegedly' supplies letters rather than doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: To gainsay is to deny or contradict a statement, so it means to disagree with it.

clue.text: Martin and Rose mostly soaked together. In this?

definitions.text: Martin and Rose mostly soaked together. In this?

indicators.note: soaked means drunk, and two tipsy companions are thoroughly mixed up together
mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the flower name is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, before trimming

explanation.surface: Two people called Martin and Rose get drenched side by side, and the clue asks what weather did it.
explanation.walkthrough: The question 'In this?' points back to 'soaked': the whole clue describes the event while its letters build the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy downpour is what leaves two people walking together wet through, so the whole clue paints the storm.

clue.text: Scot needing clothes stripped Latin American native

indicators.note: a person needing clothes has lost their outer layer, so only the inside is kept

parts.note: the inner letters of the word Scot

indicators.note: stripped means peeled of its outside, so the outer letters are removed and the core remains

parts.note: the inner letters of the word Latin

explanation.surface: A naked Scotsman meets a Latin American who has also shed his clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Latin American native' reads as one phrase, but Latin is wordplay and only 'American native' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: The coati is a raccoon-like mammal native to the Americas, so it is an animal found natively there.

clue.text: Joint lender, saving skin, hedges pound sterling

indicators.note: a hedge surrounds a field, so one piece encloses the other
saving the skin of something means keeping it whole inside, here losing the outermost letters

parts.note: a banker is a lender; drop its first and last letters
L is the pound sign, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A joint lender covers its losses and hedges its currency exposure in pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is finance jargon: joint lender, hedging sterling. 'Joint' is the definition, a body part, and the lender is a banker with the edges cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankle is the joint where the foot meets the leg, an example of a body joint.

clue.text: Turning street vehicles round makes a difference

indicators.note: turning, completed by the later word round, sends things back the other way, read right to left
round completes the opening word Turning, so the whole string is turned to face backwards

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
two vehicles: a cart and a bus

explanation.surface: Diverting traffic on a street changes things for the neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makes a difference' sounds like having an effect; here it is the arithmetic sense, taking one number from another.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic a difference is what remains after subtraction, so someone who subtracts makes a difference literally.

clue.text: Reserve supply I kept half closeted

indicators.note: half means only the first part of the following word is used, the rest cut away
read as the adverb of supple, supply means flexibly, so the letters bend into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the first half of this eight-letter word

explanation.surface: Someone admits to hiding away half their spare provisions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserve supply' looks like a single noun phrase; in fact 'supply' is an adverb, meaning suppl-y, flexibly, and signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockpile is a store of goods put aside for later use, which is a reserve.

clue.text: Swingers do it in disreputable local site

indicators.note: something disreputable is not in good order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Wife-swappers carry on at a seedy venue nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swingers' suggests partner-swapping; it means anything that swings, such as a pendulum.
explanation.definitionFit: To oscillate is to swing back and forth regularly, the motion of a pendulum or a swing.

clue.text: Cross can be sprayed, given change of heart

indicators.note: a change of heart here swaps the central letter of the word for a different one

parts.note: land that can be watered by sprinklers or channels is irrigable

explanation.surface: An aerosol can is sprayed after someone changes their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter G becomes T. 'Cross' is the adjective, meaning annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross as an adjective means angry or annoyed, and irritable means easily annoyed.

clue.text: Hard cop denied beginning pursuit

indicators.note: denied its beginning means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
a bobby is a British police officer, before losing its first letter

explanation.surface: A tough police officer is refused the chance to start a chase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pursuit' suggests a chase to go with the cop, but here it means a pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: A pursuit can be a leisure activity someone follows regularly, which is what a hobby is.

clue.text: Amateur Irish sweeper affiliated to Hearts becomes Barnet manager

indicators.note: affiliated to means attached to, so the following piece is joined on at the front

parts.note: H is the card abbreviation for hearts
A is the abbreviation for amateur
IR is an abbreviation for Irish
a brush sweeps floors

explanation.surface: An amateur Irish defender linked to Hearts, a Scottish football club, takes charge of Barnet, an English club.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnet is Cockney rhyming slang for hair (Barnet Fair), as well as a football club, so its 'manager' is what keeps hair in order. A sweeper is also a defensive football position.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairbrush manages or tidies the hair, which rhyming slang calls the barnet.

clue.text: Arrogant king doing for relations in city by poison gas

indicators.note: doing for something means standing in for it, so one piece replaces another

parts.note: CO is the formula of carbon monoxide
taken as written, before the swap
it is slang for sex, sexual relations
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A haughty monarch kills off his relatives in a town using gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relations' looks like family, but it means sexual relations, which slang calls 'it'. Inside the word city, the letters for 'it' are replaced by the chess symbol for king.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocky describes someone overconfident and self-assured to the point of conceit, close to arrogant.

clue.text: Dog bites top of Ivanka Trump's bottom. Could this have protected her?

indicators.note: a dog that bites holds something between its jaws, so a piece goes inside

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of the name
ass is American slang for bottom, apt for a Trump

explanation.surface: A dog bites a famous woman's rear, and the clue asks what armour might have saved her.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the question: a piece of armour that would have protected her. Strictly it guards the torso, not the bottom, which is part of the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuirass is a breastplate and backplate worn as body armour, so it protects the wearer.

clue.text: Retiree dines simply, entertaining thin character

indicators.note: to entertain is to host or hold within, so the words carry the answer inside them

parts.note: runs across the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A retired person eats plainly while hosting a skinny guest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thin character' looks like a person; it means the quality of being thin.
explanation.definitionFit: Reedy means slender like a reed or thin in tone, so reediness is a thin quality or character.

clue.text: More acid dispersed by college cleaner

indicators.note: dispersed by means split apart by, so one piece is driven into the middle of another

parts.note: more acid in taste is sourer
C is the abbreviation for college

explanation.surface: A stronger acid gets broken up by a college cleaning worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleaner' looks like a person; it is a pad or a product for scrubbing.
explanation.definitionFit: A scourer is a pad or powder for scrubbing pans, so it is a cleaning tool.

clue.text: Billy's inside information includes too much obtained by dubious means

indicators.note: the inside of the name means its middle letters, with the ends discarded

parts.note: the inner letters of the name Billy

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it within, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
OTT abbreviates over the top, meaning excessive

explanation.surface: Billy's insider tip involves something excessive acquired dishonestly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Billy's inside information' looks like insider trading; it splits into Billy's middle letters and gen, British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-gotten gains are acquired by dishonest or illegal methods, so the term means obtained dubiously.

clue.text: Public upset — Ashes holder lost

indicators.note: something lost has gone missing, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: to upset is to overturn
an urn holds a person's ashes, and the Ashes cricket trophy is a tiny urn

explanation.surface: The public is upset when the Ashes trophy, contested in England-Australia cricket, goes missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ashes holder' suggests the cricket team holding the trophy; it is the container for ashes.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means done openly, in plain view, which is the public sense of the word.

clue.text: Short cut taken by lad climbing Greek island

indicators.note: something taken by another is held by it, so it goes inside
climbing in a down clue means going upwards, so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: a son is a lad

indicators.note: a short version of the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to axe is to cut, before losing its last letter

explanation.surface: A boy climbing on a Greek island takes a shortcut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short cut' reads as a shortcut, but 'Short' trims the word for cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Naxos is the largest island of the Cyclades in the Aegean Sea.

clue.text: Music maker taking more from Bantock than Joubert

indicators.note: taking from a name means keeping some of its opening letters, and more says a longer stretch here

parts.note: the first three letters of the composer's name

indicators.note: than sets up the comparison, so a shorter opening stretch is kept from the second name

parts.note: the first two letters of the composer's name, fewer than the three taken before

explanation.surface: A music-maker borrows more from one composer than another.
explanation.walkthrough: Granville Bantock and John Joubert are both British composers, which feeds the musical surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A banjo is a stringed instrument, and any instrument is something that makes music.

clue.text: Explosive producer about to upset beauty in audition

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: on can mean about, concerning

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a belle is a beauty

explanation.surface: A firework maker is about to ruin a beauty contestant's tryout.
explanation.walkthrough: Alfred Nobel invented dynamite, so he was a producer of explosives.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Nobel, the Swedish chemist who founded the Nobel prizes, invented and manufactured dynamite.

clue.text: Stone Age art lacking focus bores

indicators.note: something that bores drills its way into another, ending up inside it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the focus of a word is its central point, so the middle letter goes

parts.note: taken as written, before losing its middle letter

explanation.surface: Stone Age cave art that lacks a central subject bores its viewers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stone Age art' reads as a phrase; 'Stone' alone is the definition, and 'bores' is a verb meaning drills into.
explanation.definitionFit: Agate is a banded variety of chalcedony, a semi-precious stone used in jewellery.

clue.text: 'Bubbly Buxom Brenda' wanting a duke's address

indicators.note: something bubbly is fizzing and lively, so the letters are churned into a new order
wanting means lacking, so the named letters are taken out

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, to be removed
D is the abbreviation for duke, to be removed

explanation.surface: A vivacious, curvy woman lacks a duke's address, as if in a tabloid personal ad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bubbly' is set inside the quotation marks as if part of Brenda's billing, but it is the anagram signal; the 's of duke's means 'is' here.
explanation.definitionFit: A box number is a postal reference to which replies are sent, so it serves as an address.

clue.text: Ghastly vision of extremes of panic in staff changing places

indicators.note: changing places means two items swap their positions within the word
the extremes of a word are its two ends, first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of panic
a sceptre is a ceremonial staff

explanation.surface: A frightening sight causes panic among the staff, who rush about switching positions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' suggests employees; it is the royal rod. Within that word the C and P, which are the two ends of panic, swap places.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectre is a ghost or apparition, which is a ghastly vision in the literal ghostly sense.

clue.text: Student couples ultimately avoid scam, hoax, lark and rag

indicators.note: the ultimate couple of a word is its last pair of letters, and avoiding them means cutting them off

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A student's pairs stay clear of pranks and tricks, a list of jokes and rag-week stunts.
explanation.walkthrough: Each of the four words loses its last two letters. In Britain rag week is a student fundraising festival full of stunts, which fits the student surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar is a learned person or one holding a scholarship, so a student in the academic sense.
